canonical_name: Student Journal of Business and Economics
organizer: Student Journal of Business and Economics (independent; contact via Gmail, no university/institutional affiliation disclosed on pages fetched)
eligibility_verbatim: Our journal is dedicated exclusively to high school students passionate about business and economics.
turkey_access_reasoning: No geographic or nationality restriction stated anywhere on the site pages fetched; also no explicit confirmation that international students are welcome, so capped per the evidence rule rather than assumed VERIFIED_ELIGIBLE.
international_access_notes: Contact email is a Gmail address (studentjournalofbusinessecon@gmail.com) with location given only as San Francisco, California -- no university or nonprofit affiliation is disclosed, unlike IJSCAR or Whitman Journal of Psychology. This does not disqualify it, but it is a real, worth-surfacing legitimacy signal for a reviewer to weigh.
peer_review_notes: "Every submission is reviewed by MBA/MS students from leading universities across the USA." This is graduate-student review, not faculty/PhD peer review. Recorded peer_review_explicit=true because the site itself explicitly frames this as a review process, but it should not be conflated with academic peer review in the traditional sense.
current_cycle_label: Not stated on pages fetched; site has functioning 'Current Issue' and 'Past Issues' pages indicating an ongoing, operating publication rather than a one-off.
cost_notes: No fee mentioned anywhere on the pages fetched (home page; attempted /submit, /for-authors, /faq all returned 404), and no explicit 'free to submit' statement either -- left as unknown rather than assumed, per the evidence rule.

evidence.raw_excerpt: Our journal is dedicated exclusively to high school students passionate about business and economics... Every submission is reviewed by MBA/MS students from leading universities across the USA.

notes_uncertainties: TARGET #1 FINDING: fills a real gap identified by Wave 1 -- the only dedicated economics/business-specific high school journal found. Note: broad web search also surfaced a supposedly separate 'Young Economists Journal' (youngeconomistsjournal.com), claimed by SEO blog-aggregator sites (Polygence, Aralia, etc.) to be run by the University of Birmingham Economics Society for ages 14-18 -- but independent search could not corroborate this claim at all, direct fetch failed (certificate error), and the only verifiable journal by that name is an unrelated Romanian academic economics journal (Revista Tinerilor Economisti, University of Craiova, est. 2003, not high-school-facing). That lead was NOT included here -- see rejected file. Sub-pages for submission guidelines, fees, and FAQ all 404'd on studentjournalofbusiness.com during this session, so fee and deadline remain genuinely unconfirmed rather than assumed free/rolling. Recommend a follow-up fetch of the correct submission-guidelines URL before upgrading to VERIFIED.

eligibility_verbatim: We accept submissions of previously unpublished poetry from students in grades K-12 for publication in our Cornerstone section.
eligible_grades: K-12 (not high-school-specific -- one combined section spanning kindergarten through 12th grade)
turkey_access_reasoning: No geographic restriction stated in the guidelines fetched, but international eligibility is not explicitly confirmed either, so capped rather than marked VERIFIED_ELIGIBLE.
international_access_notes: Cornerstone submissions must be accompanied by parental permission to publish if accepted. Returning contributors must wait two issues before submitting again. Work must be previously unpublished.
peer_review_notes: Editorial selection for a print literary journal section; not described as peer review.
current_cycle_label: Most recent window (January 24 - March 15, 2026) has closed; next scheduled window is September 1 - November 1, 2026.
cost_notes: "There is currently no fee for submissions to our Fiction, Poetry, and Cornerstone sections."

evidence.raw_excerpt: We accept submissions of previously unpublished poetry from students in grades K-12 for publication in our Cornerstone section... There is currently no fee for submissions to our Fiction, Poetry, and Cornerstone sections... Cornerstone submissions must be accompanied by parental permission to publish if accepted.

notes_uncertainties: TARGET #2 FINDING: the section once called 'Children's Corner' (per third-party listings like Winning Writers and NewPages, and still the name it is indexed under by search engines) has been renamed 'Cornerstone' on the publication's own current site -- the name-check requested by this task was warranted. Confirmed this is genuinely a K-12 combined section, not a high-school-specific track: a 17-18 year old's poem is read and published alongside work from elementary-age children in the same small section, with no separate high-school-only track. It is real, free, and a legitimate university-affiliated (Spalding University) literary journal credit, so it is included -- but it should be positioned to students as a lower-prestige/backup credit rather than a flagship one, and is materially weaker than Foyle Young Poets or Rattle Young Poets Anthology (both age-banded specifically toward teens) already in the corpus. Best suited to a younger high schooler (9th-10th grade) wanting an easy, real, free first publication credit.

organizer: The Poetry Society (UK), a registered charity
eligibility_verbatim: NOT DIRECTLY CONFIRMED this session (ypn.poetrysociety.org.uk and poetrysociety.org.uk both blocked automated fetch with HTTP 403 across 3 separate attempts and sub-paths -- same domain family and identical blocking pattern already documented for Foyle Young Poets in Wave 1). Per web-search results attributed to the official domain: 'Young Poets Network is The Poetry Society's free online platform for poets aged 25 and under... Young poets based anywhere in the world can take part in writing challenges and workshops.'
eligible_grades: ages 5-25 (spans and considerably exceeds the high school range; parental permission required if aged 12 or under)
turkey_access_reasoning: Per search-indexed content attributed to the official domain, described as open to young poets 'based anywhere in the world' -- capped at ELIGIBLE_WITH_CONDITIONS rather than VERIFIED_ELIGIBLE because this session could not directly fetch and quote the official page itself (403 on every attempt), consistent with the same cap Wave 1 applied to Foyle Young Poets for the identical reason.
international_access_notes: Structurally distinct from Foyle Young Poets of the Year Award (same parent organizer, The Poetry Society) -- Young Poets Network is a year-round platform of recurring themed 'challenges' and workshops with rolling publication as the prize, rather than one single annual juried competition. Entry reported as always free. If aged 12 or under, a parent/guardian permission form is required.
peer_review_notes: Editorial selection of challenge winners for online publication; described as participatory/educational ('helps young people discover new authors, techniques and ideas for writing') rather than a formal peer-review or a purely prestige-competitive process.
current_cycle_label: Platform runs a continuous rolling series of individually-timed themed challenges (e.g. a live Submittable-hosted 'Couplets Challenge' was found and fetched directly during this session) rather than one fixed annual deadline.
cost_notes: Reported as always free per search-indexed official content; the one live Submittable challenge page fetched directly during this session showed no entry fee.

evidence.raw_excerpt: Young Poets Network is The Poetry Society's free online platform for poets aged 25 and under. Young poets based anywhere in the world can take part in writing challenges and workshops, learn about the poetry world and share their work.
Submittable portal for 'The Couplets Challenge on Young Poets Network', live during this session, with an international country-selection field in the submission form and no listed entry fee.

notes_uncertainties: TARGET #3 FINDING (second dedicated poetry-only venue, distinct from Foyle Young Poets and Rattle Young Poets Anthology already in the corpus). Same organizer as Foyle (The Poetry Society, a UK charity) but a structurally different venue -- a year-round rolling platform of themed challenges rather than one annual juried award -- and a much wider age band (5-25) than Foyle's 11-17. The root domain and its /about page both returned HTTP 403 on direct WebFetch across 3 attempts, so recorded as CANDIDATE rather than VERIFIED, matching exactly how Wave 1 handled Foyle Young Poets for the same reason. One live Submittable sub-page for a specific current challenge WAS fetched directly and corroborates the platform is genuinely active right now. ALSO INVESTIGATED AND SET ASIDE (neither accepted nor formally rejected -- insufficient evidence either way): Kalopsia Literary Journal -- repeatedly blocked or empty fetches from 3 different sources (kalopsialit.org, pw.org, duotrope.com), and one secondary listing described it as 'believed to be defunct;' could not confirm poetry-only focus or current activity, so left out entirely rather than guessed. Nancy Thorp Poetry Contest at Hollins University was also investigated and found to be a strong, well-regarded poetry-only venue, but is restricted to 'high school girls in their sophomore or junior year' who are 'U.S. citizens' -- moved to the rejected file since both restrictions disqualify the Turkey-based target user.

canonical_name: International Journal of Secondary Computing and Applications Research
organizer: IJSCAR editorial board (Editor-in-Chief Dr. Maria Hwang, Fashion Institute of Technology, plus four named professors from Yale, University of Texas at Tyler, Queensland University of Technology, and Fashion Institute of Technology)
eligibility_verbatim: Every paper must include at least one co-author who is enrolled in a secondary school (equivalent to US 9th through 12th grade) at the time of submission.
eligible_grades: 9-12 (or international equivalent); at least one co-author must be a current secondary student -- multi-author work with a non-student collaborator (e.g. a mentor) is explicitly permitted
turkey_access_reasoning: No geographic restriction stated, and the editorial board itself is drawn from multiple countries' universities (US, Australia) which is a positive signal -- but explicit confirmation that non-US applicants may submit was not directly quoted on the pages fetched, so capped rather than marked VERIFIED_ELIGIBLE.
international_access_notes: Indexed on Zenodo (a CERN-operated open research repository that assigns DOIs), with Volume 2 and Volume 3 (through at least Issue 2, 2026) both published -- a genuine, sustained multi-year publication history rather than a one-off site.
peer_review_notes: "Single-blind peer review process" in which "the identities of the authors will be made known to the reviewers, but the reviewers will remain anonymous to the authors," conducted by reviewers who "hold a Ph.D. (or equivalent) in a relevant field" and are paid for reviews. A named editorial board (Editor-in-Chief plus four named professors at named universities) is a materially stronger legitimacy signal than the other CS-specific journal investigated this session (see notes below).
current_cycle_label: No single fixed annual deadline found; publication proceeds 'at next available issue,' with Volume 3 Issue 2 (2026) the latest confirmed issue -- indicating a rolling/continuous submission model across multiple issues per year.
cost_notes: "$450 USD for accepted papers only; no submission fee" -- i.e. free to submit and be reviewed, with the $450 fee applying only upon acceptance. Notably higher than comparable venues (e.g. Journal of Emerging Investigators charges $49). A 2025-cycle scholarship program existed offering the top 3 submissions $500 USD awards plus free publication, suggesting some fee-waiver/prize mechanism exists, though its exact terms for the current cycle were not confirmed (the confirmed deadline, June 30 2025, has already elapsed).

evidence.raw_excerpt: A highly-selective (approx. 30% acceptance rate), open-access journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in the field of computing and applications, with a special focus on researchers in secondary school... Every paper must include at least one co-author who is enrolled in a secondary school (equivalent to US 9th through 12th grade) at the time of submission... $450 USD for accepted papers only; no submission fee.
current secondary school student (equivalent to US grades 9-12)... The top 3 submissions will receive $500 USD [2025-cycle deadline June 30, 2025, already elapsed].
Volume 3, Issue 2 (2026) listed as the latest published issue, confirming active, ongoing operation.

notes_uncertainties: TARGET #4 FINDING (computer-science half): this is a genuinely computer-science-specific high school research journal, distinct from the broad-science venues already in the corpus (NHSJS, Curieux, Young Scientist Journal/Vanderbilt, JHSS). Chose this over 'Journal of High School Computer Science' (JHCS, highschoolcomputerscience.com), which was also investigated in depth: JHCS publishes clear and arguably even more rigorous submission guidelines (requires a public GitHub repo, reproducible code, ACM/IEEE formatting), but its /about and /editorial-board pages could not be reached (404), and no named reviewer or editor was found anywhere despite repeated targeted searching -- whereas IJSCAR has a named Editor-in-Chief and four named professors with named university affiliations, plus a multi-year, multi-issue Zenodo-indexed publication history. That is a materially stronger legitimacy signal, so IJSCAR alone was added. JHCS also charges $100 per review round for up to 3 rounds (up to $300), roughly comparable in scale to IJSCAR's $450 acceptance fee. Neither journal's fee is small for a Turkey-based family and this should be surfaced plainly to students/parents rather than downplayed. CHEMISTRY-SPECIFIC HALF OF TARGET #4: NOT FOUND. Multiple rounds of searching (general web search plus targeted queries for 'chemistry journal high school students', 'chemistry olympiad journal publish', 'Journal of Student Chemistry') surfaced only broad-science journals that include chemistry as one of several fields (JEI, NHSJS, JHSS, AJUR, AJSR, Curieux -- several already in the corpus) and never found a chemistry-only equivalent to IJSCAR. This appears to be a genuine gap in the current landscape rather than a search failure -- recommend treating this as a confirmed negative result.
